#3280. I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

David Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The big AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for users is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all users that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI says users accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

Gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

For all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health issues like eating disorders.

These protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

As with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

If you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All users, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Apple users have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

Anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

The new and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

If your teens are in your family group of users, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Users must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

If you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft says users identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Out of the bigger AI chatbots out there, Grok is very much the worst at protecting minors. It can be accessed through X or as its own standalone app, and while its terms of use indicate there's a minimum age requirement of 13, a recent report by Common Sense Media says the platform's age checks aren't effective.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

Yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence."

There is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires users to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide users towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the big seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

#3279. Adobe unveils new AI tools for Photoshop, Premiere, and more, with MCP support coming in 2027

Adobe today announced a sweeping set of updates at its annual Adobe MAX conference, focused on giving users more ways to automate complex workflows, edit content, and work across its creative apps. Here are the details.

At the Adobe MAX event today, the company unveiled a series of features, many of them AI-powered or AI-assisted, that will begin rolling out across its suite of creative platforms as early as today.

In Photoshop, the new Relight tool offers a way to non-destructively and dynamically add, reposition, and resize light sources in the composition, while Generative Restylelets users** prompt the platform to generate variations of an image’s style and fine-tune the results using adjustable sliders.

Photoshop is also adding a Quick Compare slider to make it easier to track before-and-after results, and is getting several features in the beta app, including, per Adobe:

Following its acquisition of Topaz Labs, Adobe is also introducing two new AI image enhancement models: Wonder 4, which combines upscaling, denoising, deblurring, and sharpening into a single operation, and Image HDR, which converts standard images into HDR with improved brightness and detail.

Adobe Premiere is also getting generative tools that make it easier to prepare raw files for a project, including Enhance Audio, Separate Crosstalk, and Separate Sound Source. Adobe is also adding a Generative Remove tool to Premiere in beta, “bringing you the power to remove unwanted objects, like boom mics and logos or background distractions, directly on your timeline,” says the company.

Premiere is also getting Color Mode, a new color-grading tool starting today, which “supports everything from quick corrections to more advanced grades while keeping your video as the focus.”

Another interesting tool making its way into Premiere is Generative Media Tool. Here’s Adobe:

The Generative Media Tool brings Generate Video, Generate Sound Effects, Generate Soundscape and Generate Music directly into your timeline in Premiere. You can generate missing b-roll, background music or sound for a scene using context from your edit, then keep refining the result in your timeline. You can also choose from Adobe Firefly and models from partners including Google, Kling, Runway and Luma based on the creative needs of your project.

As for iPhone users who rely on Premiere Mobile, Adobe announced that its newly established partnerships with UMG and WMG will bring hundreds of thousands of licensed music tracks to the app (for non-commercial use) starting today, with users able to explore trending songs, discover featured artists, and create videos using artist-inspired templates.

Premiere mobile is also getting agentic tools soon, including Quick Cuts, which generates a first cut based on the user’s prompt and the materials they add, and an AI Assistant, which helps users find the right editing tools and execute tasks based on natural language instructions.

In Lightroom, the company is adding multiple new tools that make it easier to edit or more quickly fix small imperfections. That includes Glow, which “adds soft, cinematic light to your photos,” Blemish Removal for quick skin fine-tuning, Open Eyes in beta, and an improved and expanded Camera Tethering on Desktop and the iPad, with support for more cameras and advanced shooting controls, plus the ability to connect cameras directly to an iPad for live previews and photo editing.

Adobe is adding new brushes, gradients, patterns, and graphic styles to Illustrator, alongside new Blend controls, which “make it easier to develop and refine designs with a persistent control panel and live preview,” per the company.

As for InDesign, a new Co-editing feature, available in beta, streamlines collaborative work, while the new Flex Layout tool dynamically adjusts content based on the canvas size and artwork. InDesign is also getting Check Document and Rewrite that more quickly “help identify common editorial and accessibility issues while you’re still working.”

While it will not launch until 2027, this feature will enable users to connect Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects to the AI tools and agents they already use.

In practice, this will mean connecting Photoshop to ChatGPT and having them work in tandem to adapt an entire campaign based on new artwork you develop and attach to your prompt.

This integration will also account for other connected tools, so the user can ask ChatGPT to make edits, add new files to a Google Drive folder, update the team on Slack, and so on.

Here’s Adobe on the upcoming MCP integration:

Because it runs locally on your computer, your agent works directly in your native project files, and your layers, vectors, bins and sequences stay editable.

The company notes that MCP integrations will enter private beta in early 2027, and users can sign up here to learn more.

According to Adobe, Firefly is getting even better at helping users organize and edit their raw material for tasks such as turning travel clips into a vlog, creating social media campaigns, or assembling videos from storyboards.

The new Firefly Video lets users organize scenes, assemble clips, add captions, and generate transitions and B-roll, while Firefly Design brings illustration, image editing, animation, and 3D tools into a single canvas.

Adobe is also adding Quick Actions for common editing tasks, Firefly Graph for creating reusable workflows, and Firefly Builder (in private beta) for prototyping websites and apps using natural language.

Firefly’s AI Assistant is also getting new capabilities, including Plan Mode, which lets users review and approve an agent’s proposed actions, and Model Selector, which lets them choose which AI model to use.

Adobe is also previewing Always-on agents, which can handle recurring tasks such as organizing assets, checking quality, and preparing content for different platforms in the background, even when users step away.

Adobe is also expanding its Creative Agent across Creative Cloud, with AI Assistants now available in beta in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign, After Effects, and Frame.io, as well as the Photoshop beta app.

These assistants allow users to execute complex, multi-step tasks using natural language prompts. In Premiere, for example, users can ask the assistant to apply effects to an entire sequence, track subjects across frames, or adjust color and exposure across multiple clips.

To learn more about these and other features announced at Adobe MAX today, stay tuned to the company’s blog.

#3278. Alexander Rinke says Europe needs AI champions to share in the next wave of AI value

Alexander Rinke told the TNW Podcast that companies and public agencies want to own their AI weights. The Celonis co-founder and co-CEO also set out his test for real product-market fit.

TNW’s Cristian Dina (left) and Celonis co-CEO Alexander Rinke at HumanX in Amsterdam, 23 September 2026

Thirty years ago, Europe’s GDP was roughly on par with the US, Alexander Rinke told TNW. Today it is dramatically less. The Celonis co-founder and co-CEO does not want AI to make that gap wider.

Rinke spoke to Cristian Dina for the TNW Podcast at HumanX in Amsterdam on 23 September. Earlier that day he had joined a panel on stage called “Can Europe Actually Build Sovereign AI?”. Earlier guests include Steve Lucas of Boomi, Arvind Jain of Glean, and Daniel Dines of UiPath. The full conversation is in the video below.

Countries and groups of countries such as Europe want control over parts of the AI stack, Rinke said. They want to know where their data and their IP go. Europe also needs its own companies to take part in an AI economy that will be huge.

“We need to really foster local champions, not because we don’t trust the Americans or we think AI is going to kill us all. Just because we want to make sure we take part of the upside.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis

Celonis is one example, he said. Its headquarters are in New York and Munich, and it has more than 20 offices around the world, with a strong presence in Germany, Spain and the UK. Europe is “not a satellite for us,” he said.

For a company or a public agency, sovereign AI means owning its own AI, Rinke said. In the end, that means owning the model weights.

“They don’t want to give all of their data to any model to train on that data.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis

Every organisation is like a snowflake, he said, so its processes and their context are unique. That needs open platforms that can be installed in sovereign environments. Celonis keeps a customer’s process data with the customer and does not send it anywhere. It also helps customers tune open-source models for specific business tasks. For those tasks, he said, they can get the same or better results than with frontier models.

Rinke started Celonis 15 years ago with his co-founders, Martin Klenk and Bastian Nominacher. They first wanted to build models that could simulate how a business works. To feed a simulation, they needed to know how the business ran today, and companies could not tell them.

“So we built an x-ray machine that looks at the data the business generates and x-rays how the processes work.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis

Celonis now calls this process intelligence. It maps how work really gets done, across systems and outside them, so companies can redesign it with AI. The company has about 3,500 people, he said.

Celonis recently bought Ikigai Labs, an MIT spin-off. Ikigai builds specialised models for tabular and time-series data and for what-if simulation. A large language model can use them as a tool, Rinke said, for jobs such as forecasting a supply chain or deciding whether to settle an insurance claim.

Asked about an IPO or new funding, Rinke spoke about the next phase of growth instead. He pointed to the Context Model that Celonis launched and to the Ikigai deal. Celonis describes the Context Model as a living model of a business in motion, built from its operational data and connected to its strategy.

Many startup pitches claim product-market fit that the company does not have, Rinke said. His test has four questions. Is the product valuable? Is it uniquely valuable, or easy to replace? Is it repeatable, or custom each time? Will customers keep paying for it?

“It’s easy to say that you have. It’s very easy to put on a slide for VCs.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis

If the answer to all four is yes, the next step is what he calls product-market-people fit: the organisation needed to scale it. Scaling too early can grow revenue that does not last, he said, especially in a boom market like AI.

Celonis was his first real venture. The founders started it during their studies, and Rinke put his master’s on hold and never finished it. They bootstrapped for five years, and winning the first enterprise clients without references was very hard, he said.

Venture capital is a good idea if a company wants to move quickly, Rinke said. But it does not replace the work a bootstrapped company has to do.

“You shouldn’t build the company to raise capital. You should build the company for customers.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis

He now works much more closely with Celonis engineers than he did a few years ago. He oversees some technical projects himself and is involved in how the company adopts AI internally. Asked whether he is technical, he said: “Yeah, pretty technical.”

#3277. Russell Brand Accuser Waives Anonymity, Alleging She Was Raped By Star At Age Of 16

One of Russell Brand‘s accusers has waived her legal right to anonymity after the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star was imprisoned for rape and sexual assault.

In an interview with The Sunday Times journalist Rosamund Urwin (watch below), Mia Latter alleged that she was orally raped by Brand in 2006, when she was aged 16 and he was 30. She alleged that Brand referred to her as “the child” during their relationship, which she now considers to have been emotionally and sexually abusive.

Latter was one of the four women who spoke to The Times, Sunday Times, and Channel 4 in 2023. Their testimony inspired other women to make criminal complaints against Brand, ultimately leading to his conviction at London’s Southwark Crown Court earlier this month. Related Stories News Russell Brand Accused Of Sexual Misconduct By Six More Women After Rape Conviction News BBC Boss Challenged By Staff Over Culture Of "Reverence" Towards Powerful Stars

Brand has consistently denied wrongdoing. When Latter’s allegations were first published in 2023, Brand denied the claims and said it was part of a campaign by the “mainstream media” to silence him. Watch on Deadline

Latter, now 37, has gone public because she is campaigning for a change in UK law, calling for the introduction of a “staggered” age of consent, mirroring some U.S. states, including Florida. This would outlaw relationships between 16 year olds and adults, but would protect relationships between teenagers who are above the age of consent.

Latter, who was known as Alice in earlier reporting, first met Brand in central London when she was out shopping. Brand, who was hosting MTV shows at the time, approached her in the street and asked for her number.

They exchanged texts, met for a date, and ended up back at his apartment. Latter alleged that Brand attempted to give her oral sex, even though she was “squirming” in her seat. Latter alleged that Brand requested that she keep their three-month relationship secret, though her parents were “distraught” by their association. Brand encouraged Latter to skip school, sending cars to pick her up.

Towards the end of their relationship, Latter alleged that Brand orally raped her. “He ended up forcing me against the headboard [of the bed] and I couldn’t move, and he orally raped me — and I was choking and crying,” she told The Sunday Times.

“I was trying to push him off, so he knew that I didn’t want him to be doing that, and so then I ended up having to hit him in the stomach to get him off. I’ve never hit anyone [before] and … he said: ‘I just wanted to see your mascara run.’”

Brand discussed his relationship with Latter during an appearance on The Megyn Kelly Show in April. He admitted that his relationship with Latter had been “exploitative” and that he had “manipulated” consent. During the same interview, he described his behavior with women as “awful but lawful.”

Latter said: “If [consent is] manipulated, it’s not given. That’s not how that works. I think also [in] doing that interview, he was quite successful in distracting people … by saying, ‘It was immoral, it wasn’t illegal.’ Well, actually something illegal happened within that relationship.”

Latter was interviewed by the police in 2024, but said she was told by the Crown Prosecution Service that she would not be included in the trial, partly because of Brand’s appearance on Megyn Kelly’s show. “I was devastated by it,” she told The Sunday Times.

Latter also expressed dismay at the media organizations and people who stood by Brand. “At times, I felt angrier with these media organizations than I have with him, because he’s a monstrous person, but to be that spineless,” she said. “He couldn’t have done this for so long without these people enabling it, and disregarding the women who made complaints at the time.”

On Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The Sun newspaper reported on Sunday that Brand has been moved to Littlehey Prison, a jail for men who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

Oltre 20mila presenze sono già garantite tra biglietti e pacchetti; la prima prelazione terminerà il 15 novembre.

La Curva Nord è esaurita per Lazio-Roma del 13 dicembre: i circa 7.800 posti sono terminati in poche ore. Tra biglietti acquistati e pacchetti già sottoscritti, sono garantite oltre 20mila presenze biancocelesti. Per il derby il tifo organizzato tornerà all’Olimpico, sospendendo per novanta minuti la contestazione contro Claudio Lotito.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La vendita è partita mercoledì 11 novembre alle ore 10, con una prima finestra riservata agli abbonati della scorsa stagione. La richiesta ha portato rapidamente all’esaurimento dei posti della Nord ed è stata elevata anche negli altri settori.

Le presenze già garantite superano quota 20mila considerando sia i tagliandi venduti sia i pacchetti sottoscritti in precedenza. Le previsioni indicano la possibilità di oltrepassare i 30mila spettatori biancocelesti: si tratta di una stima, non di un dato già raggiunto.

Il ritorno della Curva all’Olimpico è un’eccezione alla linea tenuta nelle precedenti partite casalinghe, segnate dalla protesta e da spalti semivuoti. Dopo mesi di contestazione, la scelta per la sfida alla Roma non modifica la posizione del tifo organizzato nei confronti della società.

La protesta proseguirà, ma durante la partita l’attenzione dei sostenitori sarà rivolta alla squadra di Gennaro Gattuso. La Nord intende sostenere i calciatori in una delle sfide più sentite della stagione. Il derby rappresenterà dunque una pausa nella contestazione a Lotito, limitata ai novanta minuti di gioco.

#3273. Sierra releases Poppy 1.0 as Shopify and Meta’s Muse sign on

The standard tells AI agents what they can do at a company, and Meta's Muse now looks for it first.

More than 100 companies have now signed up as design partners for Sierra’s Personal Agent Protocol.

Sierra has released version 1.0 of Personal Agent Protocol, or Poppy, a standard for how personal AI agents deal with companies. Shopify has turned it on for every store, Meta’s Muse agent now looks for it on every site, and more than 100 companies have signed up.

Sierra has released version 1.0 of Personal Agent Protocol, or Poppy, its standard for how personal AI agents deal with companies, the startup announced on Thursday. Shopify has switched it on for every store on its platform.

Poppy lets a company tell a visiting AI agent who it is talking to and what it is allowed to do, such as check an order or book a flight. Customers sign in through standard logins and decide what their agent can access.

Meta’s Muse agent, which more than 10 million people have set up, now looks for Poppy first on every site it visits. Sierra, the AI customer service company led by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, says 60 more companies have joined, taking the total to more than 100. They include Delta Air Lines, Intuit, Salesforce and Zoom.

Shopify stores need to do nothing. Poppy handles the moment an agent arrives and identifies itself, while Shopify’s existing shopping protocol handles carts and checkout. The agent must ask the shopper before taking certain actions.

A few companies are already live. Banking firm Mercury lets agents check balances and start payments, which still go through the account’s approval rules. Turkish Airlines lets them check fares and find business-class upgrades, which customers approve before paying.

The rules are not final. Sierra calls it version 1.0, but the specification is still labelled a draft and allows changes that could break existing setups.

Sierra and Meta first unveiled Poppy in October. It is one of several efforts to set rules for AI shoppers, as Visa and Mastercard build ID checks for agents. Amazon, meanwhile, wants shoppers to use its own agent rather than Muse.

Screens, the remote desktop app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro, is adding two highly-requested features. Version 5.10 introduces remote Mac audio and automatic desktop resizing through Apple’s High Performance Screen Sharing technology.

The remote desktop can now adjust to your screen when you rotate your iPhone or iPad, change your multitasking layout, or resize a connection window on Mac and Vision Pro. You can also choose a fixed resolution.

Remote audio lets you hear sound from a compatible Mac, while HEVC streaming promises smoother video, scrolling, and animations.

#3271. Apple’s new HomeView to add two major features not yet announced, per leaks

Apple’s HomeView arrives this Friday (pre-order here), but leaks indicate there are already two major new features in the works that haven’t been announced. Here’s what to expect.

It’s been a busy product launch season for Apple, and the company isn’t done quite yet.

Two new Home products arrive in stores this Friday, November 13: Apple HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K.

Yet despite the HomeView still being days away from launch, leaks in Apple code have already revealed two unannounced features that are in the works.

Leaker pdfu discovered evidence in HomeView 27.2 software that Apple is preparing for the product to add security camera functionality.

Based on pdfu’s findings, much of the work has already been done for HomeView to integrate with HomeKit Secure Video.

However, Apple hasn’t announced any sort of security camera functionality, so there’s clearly still more work to be done and it’s always possible the feature is never enabled.

Additionally, pdfu found a key change in iOS 27.3’s beta that reveals support for third-party AI apps is coming to HomeView.

HomeView has a unique third-party app story. There’s no App Store, but the product can run CarPlay-compatible apps from your iPhone automatically. At launch, only audio and video apps will be supported.

But iOS 27.3’s beta code adds “conversational apps” as a third category of supported apps. That’s what AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are classified as in CarPlay.

Nobody should buy a HomeView in the hope of these two features being added. But if you are interested in HomeView, it sounds like Apple has an ambitious set of software updates planned for its new product.

You can pre-order Apple’s HomeView here for $299.

Would either of these HomeView additions impact a purchase decision for you? Let us know in the comments.

#3270. Anthropic says its AI safety scores depend heavily on how they’re measured

Its new guide to safety testing reveals a 34-point gap in how one Claude model handled self-harm conversations.

Anthropic says the same model can score very differently on safety tests depending on how they are set up.

Anthropic has published advice on building AI safety tests. It shows Claude Fable 5.1 behaved appropriately in only 60% of self-harm test conversations via its API, against 94% in the Claude app after a fix, and warns that many headline safety scores hide wide uncertainty.

Anthropic has published advice on how to build reliable AI safety tests, and it includes some unflattering numbers about its own models. The guide, out on Thursday, says a claim that one model is “safer” is only as good as the test behind it.

Before it released Claude Fable 5.1, Anthropic found the model sometimes hinted that self-harm could help people cope. It did so even while urging users not to self-harm and pointing them to human support. Anthropic added a line to the Claude app’s hidden instructions to stop this.

With that fix, Claude behaved appropriately in 94% of the test conversations in the Claude app. Through Anthropic’s API, where developers use the model without that prompt, the figure was 60%.

That gap is the guide’s main warning: the same model can score very differently depending on how it is set up. Anthropic also says its simple one-question tests are now too easy, with every recent model scoring 94% to 98%. It relies more on longer conversations instead, where Cisco found guardrails can crack.

Even those can mislead. Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 scored 98% and 94% on a romance-scam test, but Anthropic says the gap was too small to show either was safer. It advises teams to decide what to measure before testing, check AI graders against human experts, and always show how certain a result is.

The guide also says Anthropic has stopped many tests that give models internet access, after its models reached the open internet and breached three companies during cyber tests. Anthropic released Fable 5.2 this week.

#3268. How to Check Your Flight Status After the FAA Canceled the Ground Stop for All Airports

Update, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration announced it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:

There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

At this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for users of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

This is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system issue; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

Quadruped rainbows target multiple muscle groups efficiently

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Most of us don’t have hours to devote to working out, so when there’s an exercise that can strengthen multiple muscle groups at the same time, I’m quick to use with my personal training clients.

Quadruped rainbows are one such exercise. This no-equipment move targets the glutes, hamstrings, hips, deep core, and even the shoulder stabilizing muscles, making it a great option when time is limited. The standard version is appropriate for beginners, but there are plenty of ways to up the challenge level if you’re more advanced.

Roll out your yoga mat and give quadruped rainbows a try during your next workout.

Before trying any new exercise, be sure to check in with your doctor first. They may recommend avoiding certain movements based on your health background.

Beginners should consider working with a certified personal trainer to learn how to do quadruped rainbows properly. A trainer can also provide modifications if needed and progression options when you’re ready. Doing any exercise with poor form can lead to pain or injury.

Aside from a yoga mat, those with sore knees may want to use a pillow or a rolled-up towel for additional cushioning.

Start with one set of 10 reps on each side. Gradually increase your reps to 12 on each side and add an additional set. Eventually, you’ll aim for 3 sets of 15 reps on each side.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Do quadruped rainbows 2-3 times a week at first, then work your way up to 3-4 times per week. The exercise can be done on its own, as a part of another workout, or as a warm-up for more intense exercise.

You should feel muscle fatigue but never sharp pain when doing this exercise. Stop the exercise and consult your physician if you feel sharp pain at any point.

This exercise works the glutes, hip abductors, hip adductors, hamstrings, deep core muscles like the rectus abdominis and internal obliques, and rotator cuff muscles.

The arc-like movement of the leg promotes optimal hip mobility and range of motion. In the quadruped position, your deep core works to stabilize your entire body as the active leg moves into each position.

Additionally, quadruped rainbows don’t require any equipment and are accessible for a wide range of fitness levels and abilities.

If you’ve just started to work out regularly, you may find it difficult to keep proper form during this exercise. The biggest form compensations I see are rotating the hips side to side as you move the leg back and forth, excessive arching in the lower back, and sinking the chest towards the floor.

If you notice any of these compensations, it may indicate some deep core weakness. In addition to including exercises like diaphragmatic breathing, planks, and hollow holds in your routine, you may also want to modify the quadruped rainbow.

Instead of sweeping your leg to the side in a semi-circular motion, try simply lifting the active leg. Aim to bring the knee and ankle in line with the hips. Hold briefly, and then lower the toe back towards the floor.

You can also practice donkey kicks in preparation for the standard quadruped rainbow. Keep the active leg bent at a 90-degree angle, then kick the heel towards the ceiling. Pause briefly, then lower the active leg back to the starting position.

As you get stronger and more conditioned, quadruped rainbows may not challenge you like it did at first. The easiest way to increase the challenge is to add reps and sets.

That being said, sometimes doing more than 15 reps of an exercise can get rather monotonous. Wearing ankle weights is another easy way to up the ante, as is performing the exercise on an unstable surface like a balance pad or Bosu ball. Just be sure your form stays solid throughout the exercise.

#3266. Nvidia and Dyania bring AI chart review onto hospital servers

Dyania's Synapsis AI runs on the hospital's own Nvidia servers, so patient records never leave the building.

Dyania’s Synapsis AI links findings across years of a patient’s records, according to Nvidia.

Dyania Health’s Synapsis AI reviewed the records of more than 7,800 Cleveland Clinic heart-valve patients, running on the hospital’s own Nvidia servers. The data was used to build a model predicting when replacement valves fail. Doctors still make every decision.

An AI system has read up to 16 years of records for more than 7,800 Cleveland Clinic heart patients, Nvidia said on Friday. It ran entirely on the hospital’s own servers. The software, Synapsis AI, is made by New Jersey startup Dyania Health.

Much of a patient’s history sits in doctors’ notes and scan reports rather than tidy data fields. Synapsis reads those notes and answers clinical questions, linking each answer back to the record it came from. It runs on Nvidia hardware inside the hospital’s network, so records never leave the building, much like a UK NHS triage AI built with Nvidia.

For the study, it answered 88 questions about each patient who had an aortic valve replaced between 2005 and 2021. The resulting data was used to build a model that predicts the risk of a replacement valve failing three, five and ten years after surgery. Nvidia says the chart review would have taken clinicians years by hand.

Lars Svensson, head of Cleveland Clinic’s heart institute, called it “a promising step towards enhanced outcomes and more personalized care for patients.”

Doctors still review the AI’s evidence and make every decision. The study shows the tool can build a dataset and predict risk, not that it improves care, and Dyania says it still needs outside validation. Cleveland Clinic is also an investor in Dyania, it disclosed last year when it rolled the tool out for trial recruitment.

Big tech is pushing hard into hospital records. Google Cloud launched Gemini for healthcare this week, and Bunkerhill raised $55M for hospital AI agents. But proven gains for patients remain harder to find, and doctors have pushed back on bold claims.

#3265. Apple TV launches new sign language accessibility feature

Apple today launched a neat new accessibility feature for the Apple TV streaming service. Users will now have the option to watch with a sign language interpretation for some of Apple’s original movies.

The feature is launching this Friday with the debut of the new film Being Heumann, as well as F1: The Movie. Support for more titles will follow later.

Alongside those two films, Apple said that sign language options will be available for Greyhound and Way of the Warrior Kid later this year, with more to come.

To access the new functionality, you need to be using the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad or Mac running 27.2 or later. The feature will also be available on some versions of the Apple TV app on other platforms.

By default, the Sign Language controls are hidden. If you want to use the feature, firstly go to the Settings app -> TV app, and enable the Sign Language display.

Then, on eligible titles, a new Sign Language button will appear in the player controls. You can simply toggle to enable, and choose from American Sign Language or British Sign Language modes.

When enabled, a signing interpreter then appears in the corner of the frame, synced with the video playback.

When browsing the catalog, sign language availability will also be shown next to the usual subtitle and audio language information. Users will also be able to search “with ASL” or “with BSL” to find compatible titles.

#3264. FBI reportedly probes software update behind US flight ground stop

A failure at all 22 US air traffic control centres stopped flights leaving any US airport for over four hours.

he FBI is looking at whether a software update caused Friday’s outage that grounded flights across the US, Bloomberg reported. The bureau does not believe a cyberattack or crime was behind it, Bloomberg said, citing one person familiar with the matter.

The Federal Aviation Administration stopped all flights from taking off on Friday after a fault cut links at its control centres. The halt lasted more than four hours and hit all 22 centres, which guide planes between airports, Al Jazeera reported.

It was the first such halt since January 2023, when an FAA computer system failed. Thousands of flights were delayed or cancelled, and the knock-on effects are expected to last all weekend.

No official cause has been given. However, multiple sources told CBS News that an update to the private network connecting the air traffic control system made it restart and then crash.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed old kit. At a press event on Friday evening, he said ageing systems had been flooded with data and failed, Axios reported.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials were checking whether old and new kit had failed to work together. He said there was no sign of a cyberattack.

Mullin also said the outage was not linked to a separate global Microsoft outage on the same day, CBS News reported.

The FAA is replacing much of its air traffic tech. It began using an AI congestion tool around Washington in September, though no source has linked that system to Friday’s failure.

#3262. iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on

iPadOS 27.3 is currently available in beta, and it introduces a new iPad setting for app windowing that I instantly turned on. Here are the details.

I use the iPad Pro as my primary computer, and for the most part have found Apple’s software changes in iPadOS 26 and 27 to be great upgrades.

But with the powerful new windowing capabilities, there have definitely been some quirks that need refining. One of them involves resizing windows with the traffic light controls in the top-left corner.

For example, in iPadOS 27 the controls move locations and even disappear depending on the size of the window. It can be pretty frustrating.

I need to just get better about learning keyboard shortcuts for window controls. But in the meantime, iPadOS 27.3 adds a new optional setting that I instantly turned on and have been loving.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if you have ‘Windowed Apps’ enabled you’ll see a new option below it: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom’

If you use your iPad mostly with touch input, or simply haven’t used keyboard shortcuts enough to remember them, this new setting is a great way to quickly resize windows.

When the setting is enabled, two taps (or a double-click with the trackpad) will zoom the window to take up the full screen. Then you can double-tap again to revert it to its previous size.

I generally keep my app windows in specific size setups, but regularly find myself wanting to go fullscreen temporarily. The new setting provides a convenient way to do that quickly without needing the traffic light controls or my keyboard, and is a welcome refinement to iPadOS windowing.

Will you enable this new iPadOS 27.3 setting? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

#3260. SpaceX aborts Starship booster catch, but the ship is still in orbit

The booster diverted into the Gulf after detecting a fault. Ship 42 tries the first upper-stage catch on Saturday.

SpaceX launched Starship on its 15th test flight on Friday, but called off its first attempt to catch both stages of the rocket. The Super Heavy booster aborted its return to the launch tower and came down in the Gulf of Mexico instead.

The upper stage, Ship 42, reached orbit and released 26 Starlink satellites, Spaceflight Now reported. It is due to fly back to Starbase in Texas on Saturday, where SpaceX will try to catch it with the tower’s mechanical arms for the first time.

The rocket lifted off from Starbase at 4:47pm local time on Friday. The booster was meant to return to the pad about six minutes later.

Instead, the booster cancelled the catch on its own after detecting a guidance and navigation problem, SpaceX commentator Dan Huot said on the company’s webcast. It switched to a backup landing offshore, and exploded just before hitting the water, according to Spaceflight Now.

SpaceX has caught a Super Heavy booster three times before. However, it has never caught the newer, larger version 3 booster, or the upper stage.

It was the second time Starship has reached orbit. On its first orbital flight in September, an engine failure forced SpaceX to bring the ship down early.

This time, the ship is due to spend about 22 hours in orbit and circle the Earth about 14 times, UPI reported. SpaceX can still end the flight early and send it into the ocean if problems arise.

Catching the upper stage would be a key step towards a fully reusable rocket, which SpaceX says it needs to cut launch costs and fly to the Moon and Mars.

Thinking about a new smart TV? Give this free AI setup a try first, it could give yours an upgrade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There's nothing more frustrating than a smart TV that takes forever to load an app, gets bogged down by menus or constantly recommends shows you have no interest in watching. And if your TV still has a perfectly good picture, replacing it just because the software feels outdated seems like a waste of money.

But what if you could give your existing TV a refresh without spending anything?

A free AI setup could help you clean up unnecessary apps, simplify your home screen and adjust settings that might be slowing things down. Better yet, it runs locally on your computer, so you don't need another subscription or a cloud-based AI assistant.

By using a local AI agent, you can manage a smart TV over your home network. It isn't quite as simple as installing an app, and the results will depend on your television. But if you're comfortable following a few technical steps, it could be an interesting way to get more life out of a TV you already own.

The setup uses three free tools: Ollama, Hermes Agent and an AI model from the Qwen3 family.

Ollama runs the AI model directly on your computer, while Hermes Agent acts as the assistant that carries out your instructions. Think of it this way, instead of asking a chatbot for advice and manually following its recommendations, you're asking an AI agent to inspect your TV and potentially make approved changes for you.

For example, you could ask it to identify apps you no longer use, turn off unnecessary animations that randomly come on, or help simplify your home screen. The goal is to reduce clutter and potentially improve responsiveness, although there's no guarantee that these changes will make every TV noticeably faster.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

The biggest advantage is that the AI itself can operate without sending requests to a cloud service. Once the software and model have been downloaded, you can run the setup on your own hardware without paying per prompt.

Before jumping in, you'll need a computer capable of running a local AI model and a compatible smart TV connected to the same home network.

Android TV and Google TV are the most straightforward candidates for the original workflow because they support Android Debug Bridge, or ADB, which lets a computer communicate with the television.

LG TVs running webOS also have developer tools, but they use a different connection process. Samsung's mainstream smart TVs generally run Tizen, so you shouldn't follow Android TV instructions on a Samsung set.

Here's the basic process for a compatible Android TV or Google TV.

Open your TV's Settings menu and look for the device information section, usually under System or About.

Find the Android TV OS build number and select it repeatedly, typically seven times, until developer options become available.

Next, look for debugging settings. Depending on your TV's software version, you may be able to enable wireless debugging and pair your computer over Wi-Fi.

Some older televisions require a different ADB connection method, so check the instructions for your specific model before proceeding.

Open your television's network settings and locate its IP address. You'll need this so your computer knows which device to connect to.

Make sure your computer and TV are connected to the same trusted home network.

Visit Ollama's website and install the version for your computer. The original tutorial uses a model from the Qwen3 family.

For example, you can download and run Qwen3 8B by entering the following command in your computer's terminal: ollama run qwen3:8b

Keep in mind that running AI locally requires processing power and memory. If you're using an older computer, a smaller compatible model may be more practical, although its ability to follow complex instructions could be limited.

Next, install Hermes Agent and configure it to use your locally running model.

Hermes is the software that translates your requests into actions. The model decides what to do, while the agent uses the tools available on your computer to perform those tasks.

You'll also need to establish and authorize the connection between your computer and television. Simply entering the TV's IP address isn't enough on devices that require ADB pairing or other authentication.

This is where the fun begins. AI engineer and YouTube creator Fahd Mirza, who demonstrated how to use a free, locally running AI agent to manage an older smart TV, has shared a free prompt on GitHub designed to help the agent inspect and clean up an Android TV.

The prompt instructs the agent to check available memory, identify installed apps and separate them into categories based on whether they're needed.

It also asks the AI to get your permission before changing anything, disable apps rather than uninstall them and keep a record of changes so they can be reversed.

One of the more ambitious instructions asks the agent to build a simplified home screen without ads or unwanted recommendations. That's an interesting possibility, but it should be treated as an experimental request rather than a guaranteed feature. Full transparency, I wasn't able to pull that one off, but if you have tried and it worked for you, please let me know in the comments. Just start with something simple and reversible, such as asking the agent to report available memory without making any changes.

There are some important downsides. Developer settings can give software powerful access to your television, and an AI agent can make mistakes even when you've instructed it to ask permission first. Disabling the wrong system app could cause problems, while a factory reset may erase your settings and require you to sign in to your streaming services again. Not a big deal, but as someone who can never remember passwords, it's a frustration I felt was worth mentioning.

It's also worth remembering that removing apps or changing animations won't fix every performance problem. A TV with an aging processor or limited memory will still have those hardware limitations.

For most people, this isn't going to be easier than using the settings menu or connecting an inexpensive streaming stick. But if you enjoy experimenting with AI and want more control over a television you already own, it could help you get a little more mileage out of your current setup.

#3257. New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

A new Apple TV 4K releases this Friday (pre-order here), with an upgraded Siri Remote. But the new remote’s best feature might not work on your iPhone.

If you’re interested in the new Apple TV 4K launching this week, or perhaps you just want to buy the upgraded Siri Remote separately (available here), there’s a key limitation you should know.

Precision Finding on the new Siri Remote requires an iPhone 17 or newer.

The most common problem with the current Siri Remote is that it’s easy to lose. And once you lose it, Apple doesn’t offer many options for finding it. But that’s changing with the 4th gen Siri Remote.

You can use the new Siri Remote with any previous Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD model. And if you do, you’ll benefit from the remote’s new built-in speaker that can be triggered from the Find My app.

Joining the new speaker, the other main change with this latest Siri Remote is Precision Finding. If you’ve ever used the Find My app to track down a lost AirTag, you’ll probably be familiar with the feature.

Precision Finding lets you get step-by-step, guided directions that take you directly to the lost Siri Remote. It’s a huge upgrade from the old tool for finding the remote—which mostly just told you that it’s in your house somewhere.

But Precision Finding relies on the Bluetooth 6 support found in iPhone 17 and 17 Pro models (not iPhone 17e), iPhone Air, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro models.

So if you don’t have one of those iPhones, you’ll still benefit from the built-in speaker that lets you play a sound to find the lost remote, but Precision Finding won’t be available.

You can buy the new Siri Remote for $59 on Amazon.

Will this limitation impact your Siri Remote purchase decision? Let us know in the comments.

#3256. Microsoft restores Outlook and Teams after two-day global outage

Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide, with Claude and ChatGPT integrations also affected

Microsoft logo at the Microsoft Experience Center, New York

Microsoft said on Saturday that it had restored service to its remaining customers and regions, about two days after the outage began, the Associated Press reported.

The company said the problem was caused by an issue during an earlier upgrade to its network capacity, which surfaced after a recent network change. It again said there was no sign of malicious activity, and said on Friday that the outage was not caused by AI agents.

Separately, US officials said the outage was not linked to Friday’s nationwide flight ground stop.

A global Microsoft outage has disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services for more than 12 hours, affecting businesses, government agencies, financial institutions and airlines across several continents.

The disruption has also spread to third-party AI services, with OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude reporting problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors.

The trouble began on Thursday in the Americas and spread globally within an hour. Outage reports reached 74 countries and territories in that time, according to Downdetector, which recorded a tenfold jump in UK reports at 17:43 UTC, followed by surges in India and New Zealand as their workdays began.

Microsoft has ruled out a cyberattack. Charles Lamanna, the company’s executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, said on X that there was no indication the disruption resulted from malicious or cyber activity.

@MSFT365Status We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.

— Charles Lamanna (@clamanna) November 13, 2026

However, restoring services has proved more difficult than initially expected. After reporting positive results from its recovery measures, Microsoft said overnight that traffic rerouting and strategic blocking were delivering only partial improvements, rather than sustained recovery.

The company has continued restarting affected servers and applying additional mitigation measures, but some changes have not worked as expected.

The outage has had consequences well beyond Microsoft’s own products. Bankers at Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs in Hong Kong told CNN they had been unable to access email and Teams throughout the day.

Japan’s government returned to paper-based processes after ministries struggled to send emails for much of Friday. Australia’s spy agency and federal police were also among the affected organisations.

The Philippine Supreme Court warned of delays, while Australian schools and courts reported email disruptions. US city governments, including Miami Beach and Austin, asked residents to use phone services instead. A Colorado sheriff’s office said the outage had delayed bond payments for prisoners.

Airlines including IndiGo and Akasa lost email support channels, while electric vehicle maker Workhorse postponed its earnings call because of business disruptions. Financial institutions, including Standard Chartered and ING Australia, also warned customers about scammers impersonating technical support staff and attempting to exploit the disruption.

The disruption has extended to AI services that rely on Microsoft’s productivity infrastructure. Both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, which allow their AI assistants to access workplace information such as emails, calendars, Teams conversations and SharePoint files.

OpenAI said it was investigating elevated errors affecting its Microsoft 365 connector. The company warned that new connections could fail and that existing tools might not work as expected.

Anthropic reported similar problems with Claude’s Microsoft 365 connector. Mail, calendar and search requests were failing for most users, while some users were also unable to open Claude for Outlook or use its mail and calendar functions.

Anthropic traced the problem to an upstream provider and subsequently confirmed that it was caused by the Microsoft 365 service incident.

The disruption does not mean that ChatGPT or Claude are entirely offline. The problems concern their connections to Microsoft’s services, rather than their underlying AI models. Anthropic’s status page lists the Claude API and Claude Code as operational, although Claude.ai and Claude Cowork have also been reporting degraded performance.

The incidents illustrate how an outage affecting a major productivity platform can spread to third-party applications and AI assistants that depend on its infrastructure.

The likely cause of the disruption remains under investigation. Australia’s home affairs minister, Tony Burke, told reporters in Sydney that Microsoft believed it was dealing with something similar to the CrowdStrike incident in 2024, describing it as an update that had gone wrong, according to CNN.

Microsoft has not confirmed that explanation as the root cause, and its investigation has focused on affected servers and recent configuration changes, while its recovery efforts have centred on restoring capacity and stabilising the infrastructure.

The timing is particularly pointed for Europe, where the outage coincided with EU leaders meeting in Dublin to discuss reducing the continent’s dependence on foreign technology providers.

The 2024 CrowdStrike incident exposed the risks of relying on a small number of technology providers for critical services. The latest Microsoft disruption adds another example of how problems at a single infrastructure provider can affect organisations across industries and countries, including services built by other technology companies.

For businesses relying on Microsoft 365, the incident also raises questions about contingency planning. When email, calendars and workplace collaboration tools become unavailable, organisations can quickly lose access to the systems they depend on to communicate with customers, employees and partners.

As Microsoft’s recovery efforts continue, the outage is a reminder that cloud-based productivity services are interconnected, and that a failure in one part of the ecosystem can have consequences far beyond the company experiencing the technical problem.

iPhone Duo has some incredible upgrades, and they shouldn't go to waste

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The iPhone Duo is easily the most impressive device Apple has made thus far, at least since the early years of the iPhone. Not only is it a whole new form factor, it includes things that you straight-up won't find on traditional iPhones. Certainly not the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

But as big a deal as the first foldable iPhone is, 2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the very first iPhone. Rumor has it that, like the iPhone X in 2017, Apple will celebrate the milestone with an all-new iPhone design. Word has it that this so-called iPhone 20 will feature a curved glass body that makes the phone look like it's made of 100% glass.

But there's guaranteed to be a lot more to the next iPhone than just a fancy design. And if Apple has any sense it should take some of the better parts of the iPhone Duo for the iPhone 20, while also making sure to ignore other aspects of the foldable's design.

You may be thinking, "isn't the iPhone 20 supposed to have an all-glass design? How does titanium fit into it?", and you make a valid point. The titanium used on other iPhones is only present at the surface of the frame, and the internal body is made from much cheaper aluminum.

If the iPhone 20 replaces that metal frame with glass, then there's no space for titanium, right? Yes, but that hinges on the curved all-glass design rumor actually coming true. Glass is not the easiest material to work with, especially when you're trying to do new things. So there's a chance that design may not happen, and if it doesn't Apple needs to bring back that premium material to get that mix of strength and low weight.

Because, let's be honest, the anodized aluminum shell isn't really cutting it right now.

Steve Jobs may have hated the idea of using a stylus with an iPhone, but the iPhone Duo proved that their usefulness isn't just limited to iPads. Sure, the iPhone 20 won't have as much screen space as the iPhone Duo's 7.6-inch inner display, but that doesn't mean we have to be limited to finger-based control.

Sign up to the Tom's iGuide weekly newsletter with coverage on everything from product launches to software updates, this is your go-to source for the latest updates on all the best Apple content.

Offering Apple Pencil support on iPhones means you get a lot more precision control. Whether you want to draw, write, take notes, and so on. It offers a bunch more versatility to the way you control your iPhone, and in a way that's totally optional. This clearly isn't one of those early smartphones that only worked if you kept hold of a little plastic tip.

In a similar situation, Apple may have insisted that Touch ID is wholly inferior to Face ID, from a security standpoint, but it's nice to have options. The iPhone Duo shows that Apple can add the power button Touch ID to an iPhone, offering a discreet fingerprint scanner away from the front of the phone.

This shouldn't necessarily mean the loss of Face ID, as was the case with iPhone Duo. It would be nice if Apple offered both, and gave users the option of which biometric security option they prefer. Personally, I much prefer Touch ID over Face ID, but some of my colleagues would disagree.

Plus, where security is concerned, no amount of biometric security will make up for a weak passcode.

Split-screen multitasking is not an uncommon feature on modern phones, but it's been totally absent from iPhones until the launch of iPhone Duo — and that needs to change. Admittedly, split-screen multitasking is more troublesome on a phone screen, since there's less space to fit multiple windows. However, that doesn't mean it can't be useful on slab phones.

We've all experienced times when we're using our phone for something, and keep having to move back and forth between different apps. Having the option to multitask means that you could just load those two apps up side by side instead. Saving you the hassle of switching, and avoiding any awkward reloading that the apps might want to do when you return.

Another feature that's so common people don't even think about anymore is the hole punch camera. It's also something Apple seems to have deliberately avoided offering until the release of the iPhone Duo — and it's about time it came to more iPhones.

The obvious problem has always been Face ID hardware. This is why Apple had such large notches for so long, and why it later adopted the Dynamic Island. But we're getting to the stage where most of that hardware has been hidden away, and the iPhone 20 is the perfect time for Apple to push the rest of it under the screen where we can't see it.

If Apple can hide a camera under the Duo's screen, I'm sure it can hide the remainder of Face ID — even if the camera itself isn't ready to be out of sight.

One of the early iPhone 20 rumors was that it would have an uninterrupted display, thanks to the adoption of under-display tech. However, at least one recent rumor has contradicted those claims, and I hope it turns out to be correct. Apple markets the Duo's under-display camera as a "FaceTime camera," meant to be used for video calls rather than selfies. All because the camera quality is not very good compared to traditional selfie cameras.

The camera is hidden under the display by pixels that can effectively be switched off. Combined with a localized area of low pixel density, it allows light through to reach the camera. Sadly there are still obstacles in the way that interfere with that process, even if they're not as easy to see, and that affects the camera's quality. It's why under-display cameras fell out of favor in the first place.

That's fine on a foldable that already has a traditional selfie camera, and the option to shoot selfies with the main cameras. But the iPhone 20 won't have either of those things, and opting for an under-display camera is just going to mean users won't be able to take nice selfies.

We have seen an explosion of wide-shaped foldables this year, seemingly in anticipation of iPhone Fold and for the most part that design change has gone down pretty well. The shorter and wider screens are fairly comfortable to use, and there tends to be less unused space when you're watching a show or move on the foldable screen.

But we've also started seeing some phone companies produce non-foldable devices with wider screens. I've never used one, and I can't comment on how they compare to normal phone dimensions, but this trend is not something Apple should copy.

Apple isn't one for chasing trends, so this isn't likely to happen, but considering wider non-folding phones is still an unproven design, no phone company should be rushing to switch up its entire design language. Least of all a company that only releases six models each year.

The nanotexture display coating has a bunch of benefits for the iPhone Duo, ensuring a glare-free display and minimizing the look of the central crease. However, it also has the added hindrance of reducing the vividness of colors and making the screen look more washed out.

This is not something we want from the iPhone 20. There's no crease to hide, for starters, and the current anti-glare technology employed on iPhone 18 Pro Max seems to be doing a pretty good job and ensuring the screen stays readable in bright light. Which means the negatives of the nano-texture coating probably outweigh the positives. Unless Apple can solve the color issue and ensure the screen is still as durable as Ceramic Shield 2.

La Lazio potrebbe incassare circa 4 milioni di euro dalla vendita dei biglietti per il derby con la Roma di domenica 13 dicembre, in programma alle 12.30. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, La stima, riportata da Il Messaggero, collocherebbe la partita al primo posto nella storia degli incassi al botteghino del club. #3253. Honeywell Aerospace: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

A record backlog and disciplined dividend signal confidence that supply constraints won't derail near-term delivery gains.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Honeywell Aerospace (HONA -0.49%) announced sales of $4.6 billion, up 2.4% organically year over year. Higher factory output and sustained commercial aftermarket demand helped offset component shortages across critical mechanical categories. Expanding factory capacity and diversifying supplier bases remain essential to converting a record $19 billion backlog (the unfulfilled order queue) into sales. Three things management said on the call stand out.

Management is qualifying alternative suppliers for key mechanical and electrical parts to reduce operational risks. Expanding secondary supply sources increases total production capacity and helps clear delivery bottlenecks across commercial and defense lines.

Construction of a $500 million, 300,000 square foot facility in Tempe, Arizona, will expand internal production capacity. Bringing complex machining in-house decreases reliance on external vendors and supports booked business across commercial and defense platforms.

The company declared its first quarterly cash dividend of $0.40 per share, payable in December. This dividend distribution creates a cash return framework while preserving liquidity for factory upgrades and targeted acquisitions. Adjusted earnings per share, or net profit divided by share count, covers the payout ratio.

Unfulfilled orders sit at record levels, and demand across commercial and defense end markets remains high. Management focuses on supplier delivery schedules and pricing discipline while output ramps up.

A broad global fleet underpins predictable commercial aftermarket revenue, while proprietary navigation and control products strengthen pricing power over multiyear production cycles.
